title: The Money Box
summary: On top of the nursery wardrobe sat an enormous earthenware pig with a slit in its back. It was stuffed to the brim with silver and copper coins, so full that it could no longer rat...
full_text:
On top of the nursery wardrobe sat an enormous earthenware pig with a slit in its back. It was stuffed to the brim with silver and copper coins, so full that it could no longer rattle.

The clay pig looked down upon the dollhouse, the rocking horse, and the tin soldiers with haughty contempt: "I am worth more than all of you put together; I could purchase ten nurseries!"

One evening, while leaning forward in pride, the clay pig lost its balance, tumbled from the wardrobe, and smashed into a hundred shards upon the floor! The coins rolled under beds and into corners.

The children gathered up the money to buy new toys, and the broken shards of the proud money box were swept into the dustbin, while a fresh clay pig was placed on the shelf to start the cycle anew.
moral: Pride based upon hoarded wealth shatters into useless shards in an instant.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Money Box"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
